reason: Re-opened via packet.js veda 37 --verse 3.48.2. Sāyaṇa: yoṣā = yuvatir Aditiḥ; mahaḥ pituḥ = janakasya Kaśyapasya; dame = sūtikāgṛhe; agre = stanyadānāt prāk; pari āsiñcat = tavāsye parito akṣārayat. The paraphrase is carried in full; Wilson 3.48.2 agrees. Plain sense matches hymn 3.48 (newborn Indra longing for Soma, v.1 and v.3). verse.js ok at [281,2]; entry-check ok, 43 words. Only a phrasing note: Kaśyapa’s birth-chamber could be misread as the room of Kaśyapa’s own birth, though Sāyaṇa means the lying-in chamber in Kaśyapa’s dwelling; not a misattribution.
better: Optional rewording: the dwelling as the lying-in chamber in Kaśyapa’s house (sūtikāgṛha, dame of pituḥ Kaśyapasya), to avoid reading birth-chamber as the place of Kaśyapa’s birth.
